title: Foodborne Check Code tour
description: Inspect, verify, apply, and exercise the foodborne form's visible event-driven Check Code.
prerequisite: Import the Foodborne Outbreak Investigation example project. Its form includes the Check Code source; no code runs while you inspect it in Form Designer.

steps.title: Separate Check Code from analysis programs
steps.instruction: Check Code controls data-entry events and field behavior. It is intentionally separate from the Classic Analysis .pgm7 command tour.

steps.title: Open the Check Code Editor
steps.instruction: Select Check Code to inspect the complete source stored with this form. Opening the editor does not execute it.

steps.title: Review the event program
steps.instruction: Read the DefineVariables, Form, Page, Record, and Field blocks. The case_status After event conditionally highlights and requires onset_date, then moves focus to it.

steps.title: Verify the complete source
steps.instruction: Select Verify Source. Every field and variable reference must resolve before Apply becomes available; rejected source never runs partially.

steps.title: Apply the verified Check Code
steps.instruction: Select Apply Check Code. This saves the reviewed source into the current in-browser form; it does not submit data or call an external service.

steps.title: Exercise the form events
steps.instruction: Open Enter Data. A titled Page Before Yes/No dialog demonstrates event timing and typed assignment. Choose Yes, then select OK to continue.

steps.title: Trigger conditional field behavior
steps.instruction: Enter Confirmed in Case Status and leave the field. Check Code opens the Clinical page, highlights Onset Date in yellow, makes it required, enables it, and moves focus there.

steps.title: Review the visible effect
steps.instruction: Confirm that Onset Date is highlighted and required. Choosing a different status and leaving Case Status removes the highlight and required state. Execution remains recorded in the project audit log.

steps.title: Exercise named page navigation
steps.instruction: Enter an Interview Date and leave the field. GOTOPAGE ExposureLocation closes the Clinical page event, opens the destination page event, and reveals the exposure and location fields.

steps.title: Review the active page
steps.instruction: Confirm that ExposureLocation is the active form page. Page transitions and their bounded Check Code effects are retained in project audit history.
